title.purpose: The h2 section heading. Uppercase, tracked, slate.

body.purpose: Prose and control text. The reading column stays under 68 characters.

button.purpose: Every action label, flush left in any button wider than its text.

label.purpose: A field label, a table header, a term in the profile register.

mono.purpose: Anything the engine matches exactly: a stamp, an id, a hash, a version, a role name, CEL, or a column of figures.

shadows.name: shadow-md
shadows.purpose: The account menu popover and the dialog. The only two on-page surfaces that leave the page.

shadows.name: shadow-lg
shadows.purpose: A deeper top-layer surface. Derived from the current scheme's ink, so it stays correct in dark mode.

motion.name: none
motion.purpose: The system declares no motion tokens. State changes are instant: a hover wash, an active darken, a focus ring. No transition, no easing curve, no duration token exists in tokens.css.

breakpoints.name: narrow
breakpoints.purpose: Below this the shell header wraps, the nav takes its own row, and the profile register drops to one column.

breakpoints.name: reading-column
breakpoints.purpose: The shell screen cap. A participant reads, so the column stays narrow.

breakpoints.name: tool-surface
breakpoints.purpose: The reporting screen cap. An operator scans, so the surface goes wide.

narrative.overview:
Detent moves a case through explicit states. The interface is the record of that movement. Two devices carry the whole identity. A ruled row holds the case. A stamp marks the state it reached.

Nothing floats. No surface pretends to be a card when it is a row in a register. Alignment and rules organize the page. Shadow, color and radius do not.

The screen prints two kinds of value. Prose takes the written face. A value the engine matches exactly takes the mono face. That split is a signal, not decoration.
keyCharacteristics: Zero radius, everywhere, with no exception.
Two rule weights, and nothing between them.
One accent, used as a stamp rather than as a paint.
Machine values in mono, prose in the written face.
Flush-left alignment, including inside a wide button.

rules.name: The Stamp Rule
rules.body: The accent marks state and one primary action per screen. It never becomes the ground under content.

rules.name: The Five Tones Rule
rules.body: A stamp has five tones and no sixth. Adding one is a design change, not a screen decision.

rules.name: The Never Green Rule
rules.body: A settled case prints in ink. Success never turns green. A destructive action stays outlined in the accent and never turns red.

rules.name: The Role Rule
rules.body: A component reads a semantic role, never a ramp step and never a hex. The three flag tokens are the only exception.

rules.name: The Machine Face Rule
rules.body: A string takes mono only when you can name the reason. Otherwise it takes the written face.

rules.name: The Tracking Floor Rule
rules.body: A tracked label stays at 11px or above. Its uppercase tracking must survive umlauts and eszett.

rules.name: The Long German Rule
rules.body: German runs up to 40% longer than English. No control derives its width from the English label. No stamp takes a fixed width: a two-line stamp is correct, a clipped one is not.

rules.name: The Escape Hatch Rule
rules.body: A shadow marks an element that left the page. On the page there is no shadow, at rest or on hover.

rules.name: The Zero Radius Rule
rules.body: Every corner is square. No size, no state and no surface earns a curve.

dos: Do give a screen exactly one filled primary action.
Do print a machine value in mono. That means an id, a hash, a version, a role name, CEL, or a figure in a column.
Do name a state with a stamp in one of the five tones.
Do style a state from the attribute the DOM already carries: [aria-current="page"], [aria-expanded="true"], :disabled, :focus-visible.
Do name a class prefix-block-element, one hyphen per level, with a variant as a suffix class.
Do wrap a row's identifying content in a real control.
donts: Don't add a sixth stamp tone.
Don't read a primitive or a hex from a component. Read a role.
Don't style another area's prefix. Move a shared motif into shell/.
Don't turn success green, or a destructive action red.
Don't put a shadow on a resting surface, or on a hover state.
Don't report an error as a toast, or let an empty table stand in for one.
Don't size a control from its English label.
Don't turn a state into a class name.
